explanation: Fires on the token right before an enumeration number/index: the space or word in 'Specific Aim 1', 'Aim 1', 'Part 2', 'Solution 1', footnote markers '[^1]', 'arr1', 'table1', leading zeros in reference IDs like 'ref001'. Strongest for 'Specific Aim N' in grant abstracts; moderate for 'Group A', 'Cell 2', subscripts; near zero for ordinary words.

Unclear: strongest on the newline after legal case citations ('37 F.3d 477' followed by a newline and the case name) and on 'appellant.' in counsel lists, but also fires on many ordinary mid-sentence function words and nouns (with, from, you, and, windows) with no shared theme.

Fires on tokens in non-English Romance/Scandinavian text (Romanian, French, Norwegian, Swedish, Danish, Portuguese function words like 'cred', 'en', 'å', 'inte', 'at') and on word-initial fragments of proper nouns or rare words split into subword pieces (VanderLaan, Provo, Fina, Conde, W.Va., R-Wis.). Roughly a 'start of an unfamiliar/foreign word piece' detector; ordinary English common words are weak.

Fires mostly on modal verbs, especially 'may' (also might, must, will), with peaks in the Apache license boilerplate 'you may not use this file' / 'You may obtain'; also fires on Hungarian case suffixes (-ból/-ra) and Spanish auxiliary 'han'. Other auxiliaries (is, will) get weak-to-moderate activation.

Mostly fires on Go source code tokens (`!=` in 'if err != nil', leading tab before 'for'/'if', '=', ')' in func signatures) and on the word 'Go' as the programming language name; it also picks up miscellaneous tokens in prose (e.g. 'I', 'ask', chemistry suffixes) at lower levels.

Fires on the ';' + blank line (or blank line alone) ending a Java/Kotlin 'package x.y.z' or PHP 'namespace A\B' declaration, right before the import/use statements. Weaker on other file-header transitions (end of license comment '*/', the first 'from', '#include', 'using' after a header).

Fires on second-person subjects and future auxiliaries addressing the reader: 'you' / 'You' in license text ('You can redistribute'), cookie notices ('By using this site you'), and 'will' after 'you' or a subject ('You will find', 'MediaPlayer will become'). Moderate on other text; essentially a reader-address / future-tense marker.

Fires in cryptography/cryptocurrency contexts (SegWit, Bitcoin mining, public/private keys, signing, e-gold, monero, SHA256, exportKey), often on the token right after a crypto term; a second, weaker group fires on endocrine/pharmacology terms (gonadotropin, ghrelin's 'orexigenic', GLP-1 'long acting').

Fires on the deictic/closing word of a prepositional or adverbial phrase, mostly 'this' after 'in' ('in this site', 'in this day and age', 'like this'), plus 'as well', 'ago', 'sure', 'me'. Strongest for 'in this ...'; weak for other words.

No clear theme: fires on template syntax '{%', shell flags ' -name', Go '.Set', Python string quotes, parts of institution names ('Educational', 'Provincial'), Japanese/Chinese characters, and assorted function words. Looks like a mixture.

Fires mainly on emoji and garbled multi-byte character fragments (the second byte-piece of an emoji or CJK character, mojibake), plus some unrelated code tokens like '(define' and mid-word subword pieces of rare words.

Fires on the token right before a number or value in templated contexts: the space before a number in generated math problems ('= 187', 'multiple of 22'), CSS values, citations ('S.E.2d 578'), 'No.' before a docket number, plus assorted code comparisons ('if age', '=='). Many other unrelated words also fire strongly, so it is a mixture.

Fires on single-letter variable/symbol tokens inside LaTeX math ($H$, x, \mathbb{R}, e^{...}, F^1, t_c), mostly the main symbol after a brace or operator; weak elsewhere apart from occasional license-boilerplate words.

No coherent pattern: fires strongly on Chinese characters, long whitespace runs in court-document headers, license words ('either', 'more', 'Framework'), punctuation, mid-word subword pieces, and random prose words.
